sources.calendar.holidays: Opened: 5 U.S.C. 6103 (law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/5/6103) for the federal list and Ohio Revised Code 1.14 (codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-1.14, read via Internet Archive copy; the page says last updated July 23, 2021) for the Ohio list of 'legal holidays': the Ohio list is the same eleven days (New Year's, MLK, Washington-Lincoln, Memorial, Juneteenth, Independence, Labor, Columbus, Veterans, Thanksgiving, Christmas), plus any day appointed by the governor or President (not modelled). sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.

sources.tenancy.possession: Ohio Revised Code 1923.04: three days' notice to leave the premises before an action in forcible entry and detainer may be filed, for rent unpaid when due; after judgment a writ of restitution is carried out by a bailiff or sheriff, commonly within about ten days (to confirm: recalled, the Code not opened). plan_months 0: Ohio's courts order possession and set no plan to pay (a PLACEHOLDER for their practice). The police stand for the bailiff. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 3930: the tenant was present at 177 of 450 first hearings observed in Cleveland Housing Court in 2018-19 (Case Western Reserve University, The Cleveland Eviction Study, 2019, opened 2026-10-12; one city's court, used for the state). plan_consider 'none': Ohio's statute gives the court no plan to set (recalled, to confirm); mediation, which some courts offer and which ends some cases in an agreement to pay, is not built. 2026-10-16: ORC 1923.04, 1923.06 and 1923.13 could not be opened (codes.ohio.gov refused the connection, Justia returned 403): still recalled, to confirm.
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: US Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics 2023: 508,777 firms of age 0 over 5,593,727 firms = 9.10% (exit 523,958, 9.37%) (https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/bds/tables/time-series/2023/bds2023.csv and bds2023_fa.csv, opened 2026-10-16: no longer 'to confirm'). National. Ohio's establishment entry rate is 8.707% against 10.608% for the United States (bds2023_st.csv; Ohio had 167,526 firms and 13,461 firm deaths, 8.0%): scaled by that ratio Ohio's firm entry is about 750 (an inference, not published; not applied). It counts employer firms only, so it understates births of businesses without employees. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Starting a business of one"): the generator turns it into a monthly chance for those who could start a business of one (in the labour force, of working age, with the savings for its stock), from the businesses the town has: births a year at this rate, over those people. Most real births are businesses with no employees, which is the only kind that can be started here without premises.
sources.employment.hours: Employment at will: an employer may cut hours or pay going forward without consent and owes only wages for hours worked (FLSA 29 USC 201 ff; to confirm; Ohio Rev. Code ch. 4113 and 4111 not opened). The federal WARN Act counts a cut of more than half the hours for six months as an employment loss only for employers of 100 or more (20 CFR 639.3, opened 2026-10-13); the town's firms are smaller, so it is not modelled. The 40-hour week is the FLSA's overtime threshold. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first. 2026-10-16: no Ohio law requires reporting-time pay, minimum shift pay or advance schedule notice, or notice before cutting hours (summaries of Ohio labour law from search: secondary; ORC ch. 4111 and 4113 not opened): the zeros agree. Ohio paydays are semi-monthly or at least twice a month by statute (ORC 4113.15; DOL, State Payday Requirements, https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/payday), so the 14-day pay period is a simplification.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Employment at will: no statutory notice or severance for an individual redundancy in Ohio or federally (the WARN Act's 60 days applies only to mass layoffs at employers of 100 or more, and is left out). The law is published empty of figures: an employer owes what its agreements say (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (9.7% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (5.1%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (10.4%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (8.2%). goods: a consumer problem (29.9%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16 (not applied): Policy Matters Ohio estimates about 217,000 workers a year with minimum wage violations, about 4.2% of Ohio's 5.196 million wage and salary workers (2019, an estimate by EPI's method; secondary), 1.6 times the 255 here, and the Wage and Hour Bureau had 2,227 complaints by 4 October 2025 (snippet): minimum-wage violations only. PUCO: about 13,185 complaint investigations across all utilities in 2022, about 0.26% of about 5.0 million electric customers a year (annual reports, search; the FY2024 PDF returned 404): complaints, not wrong bills. pay_short_by_bps 500: the only quantified US figure found is 15% of earnings lost by workers in low-wage industries in Chicago, Los Angeles and New York in 2008 (Bernhardt et al., Broken Laws, Unprotected Workers, NELP 2009, summary), across all violations, urban and old: not applied; stays a PLACEHOLDER. bill_over_bps, goods_faulty_share_bps, repair_hours: no figure found. put_right_on_asking_bps: the Wage and Hour Bureau found for the worker in 78% of investigated claims and about 30 to 45% of determined sums were paid (Policy Matters Ohio, via search): findings and payments after a regulator's finding, not 'asked and put right'.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16 (not applied: no like-for-like figure): Ohio's SNAP case and procedural error rate for 2024 was 33.28% of sampled denials and terminations (USDA FNS, SNAP QC CAPER FY2024, https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/sites/default/files/resource-files/snap-fy24QC-CAPER.pdf, opened) and counts any procedural error (a late notice), the payment error rate 9.01% of benefit dollars (underpayment 1.34%) (FY2024 PER); the national reversal rate of lower-authority unemployment appeals 28.7% (search snippet). None is of qualifying claims wrongly refused; 478 stays the fitted stand-in.

sources.support.payments: [The pension:] Social Security retirement benefit: the average retired worker's benefit is about $2,071 a month from January 2026 after the 2.8% cost-of-living adjustment (Social Security Administration, announced 24 October 2025; reported by https://www.advisorperspectives.com/articles/2025/10/25/us-retirees-get-2-8-increase-2026-social-security-checks and others; the SSA fact sheet returned 403, so the figure is to confirm at https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2026.html). Paid monthly (every 30 days here), from the full retirement age; an average benefit stands in for the formula (a worker's benefit depends on 35 years of earnings; spouses', survivors', Medicare and SSI left out). [The payment to those out of work:] Unemployment compensation: placeholder of $400 a week ($800 a fortnight), estimated from Ohio's rule that the weekly benefit is about half of the claimant's average weekly wage up to a maximum of $624 for a claimant with no dependents in 2026 (Ohio Department of Job and Family Services; maximum reported by search results such as https://remotelaws.com/unemployment/us-states/ohio/, not primary, to confirm at https://jfs.ohio.gov); typical wages above give half-pay of $310-440 a week. Lasts at most 26 weeks in Ohio (Ohio Revised Code 4141.30; to confirm): the profile has no time limit (a structural gap). Open from age 18 (no age rule in the law; the other profile starts at 22 for a youth-allowance reason). Work-search and wage-history tests left out. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. The payments for those out of work end the year before the profile's retirement age (to_age): the rule the generator applied to every profile until now, written into the payment, where it can be changed. The pension is paid from Social Security. UN-FOLDED: the placeholder of $400 a week is now the rule this note gives: about half of the claimant's previous weekly wage, no more than the maximum of $624 a week ($1,248 a fortnight), for at most 26 weeks (182 days), for someone with wages on record (the employers' reports of each worker's pay). Previous pay is the mean of the monthly pay reported for the person. Nobody has a record on the first day of a run, so those out of work at the start are paid nothing until they have worked; once a payment has run its 26 weeks it is not claimed again until the person has worked. Not set: how much work history is needed (`who.record.months`, `within_months`; the note gives no figures), dependents' higher maximum, the work-search test.

sources.public_finance.income_tax: A combined schedule on gross income for a single resident, 2026. Federal: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 (tax year 2026 inflation adjustments; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf, opened): standard deduction $16,100; single brackets 10% to $12,400, 12% to $50,400, 22% to $105,700, 24% to $201,775, 32% to $256,225, 35% to $640,600, 37% above; each band starts $16,100 higher in gross income. Ohio: a flat 2.75% above $26,050 for tax year 2026 (Ohio Legislative Service Commission / Department of Taxation material on HB 96 of 2025, as returned by search; not opened; the quoted '$332 plus 2.75% of income above $26,050' suggests a small base amount that is not modelled; to confirm), added from $26,050. levy_bps 765: the employee's FICA, Social Security 6.2% and Medicare 1.45% (IRS; the 2026 wage cap of $184,500 per the SSA fact sheet, not modelled). Left out: Ohio's municipal income tax (1-3% of wages, the main revenue of Ohio municipalities), school-district income taxes, credits (earned income, child), itemised deductions. Structural gaps: no credits, no wage cap, no separate local tax. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). The income tax keeps the author's combined federal and state schedule on gross pay. UN-FOLDED: the levy of 7.65% that stood for FICA is its two parts as this note gives them, each paid to its own fund: Social Security 6.2% of pay up to the 2026 wage cap of $184,500, and Medicare 1.45% of all pay. The employers' report of the income tax names each worker and their pay (employers report each worker's wages to the state): the record unemployment compensation is reckoned from. Not expressed: the municipal income tax (the note gives a range, 1 to 3% of wages, and no rate for this town; it would be a charge with `paid_to: "town"`, which the generator pays into the town's own account), school-district income taxes, credits (a credit paid out as money needs a yearly assessment, which does not exist).

sources.justice: The tribunal is the local court of first instance (an Ohio municipal or county court: small claims, civil and eviction ('forcible entry and detainer') dockets; Ohio Revised Code ch. 1923 and 1925; hearing dates 5-15 days after service for an eviction and 15-40 days for small claims; recalled and to confirm). hearing_after_days: three weeks, a placeholder carried over. pay_within_days, apply_after_days: placeholders. challenge_bps: the share of tenants given an unlawful rent increase who go to court, and apply_bps: the share of workers owed wages who pursue a claim (placeholders: few do; Ohio wage claims go to the Ohio Department of Commerce, Wage and Hour Bureau, or to court; to source). Enforcement of an unpaid money judgment by garnishing a bank account or wages (ORC ch. 2716; to confirm). 2026-10-16: hearing_after_days 28 (was the placeholder 21): the small claims trial 'the fourth Wednesday from filing' at the Upper Sandusky Municipal Court, a scheduled date, the same source as frictions.venues. Eviction hearings 5 to 15 days after service (ORC 1923.06) were not opened (codes.ohio.gov refused the connection).
sources.education: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates, Wyandot County, Ohio (county seat Upper Sandusky; a rural county of 21,598 people), table B15003, read through the Census Reporter API (https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/latest?table_ids=B15003&geo_ids=05000US39175, opened). attainment: people 25 and over (15227): no high school diploma 5.2%, high school or GED 47.7%, some college 17.5%, associate 10.0%, bachelor's or above 19.6%, as years of schooling 10, 12, 13, 14, 16 (the years are a placeholder mapping). students_per_teacher: 16.4 pupils per teacher in Ohio's public schools, fall 2022 (NCES, Digest of Education Statistics 2023, Table 208.40, https://nces.ed.gov/programs/digest/d23/tables/dt23_208.40.asp, opened). teacher_wage_per_pay_period: $69,680 a year, mean wage of elementary school teachers (except special education) in the West Northwestern Ohio nonmetropolitan area, May 2025 (BLS OEWS series OEUM390000100000025202104, https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/, opened), over 26 fortnights. school_ages 5 to 17 (compulsory 6 to 18 in Ohio Revised Code 3321.01; kindergarten from 5), school_days_per_year 180 (minimum hours, ORC 3313.48): tried https://codes.ohio.gov, which did not connect from here, so these remain recalled, to confirm. hours_per_day 6.5: placeholder. return_per_year_bps: about 9% (Card 1999, 'The Causal Effect of Education on Earnings', Handbook of Labor Economics 3A; estimates run 6-15%; recalled, to confirm), applied linearly in the time a task takes (docs/behaviour/education.md). max_years: the skill scale's top (placeholder).
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot (carried over). The landscape around the town (margin_cells, block_cells, shares_bps, woodland_patches): placeholders for a farming township in glaciated western or north-western Ohio, mostly cropland (corn and soybeans) with woodlots and stream corridors; shaped by the NLCD land-cover mix of rural Ohio counties (recalled, not opened; to confirm at https://www.mrlc.gov). The covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; old-field scrub to woodland in about 40 years; to confirm for Ohio), the pollution figures (agricultural runoff, per farmland cell, carried over), survey_hours_per_ha, survey_staff and spin_up_years are placeholders carried over.
sources.nature.species: Real species of the region, with figures mostly placeholders and each to confirm. Eastern box turtle (Terrapene carolina carolina): a species of conservation concern in Ohio (Ohio Division of Wildlife, state-listed species, pub 5356, https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/ohiodnr.gov/documents/wildlife/state-listed-species/Pub%205356%20Ohio%20Listed%20Species_R0722.pdf, found in a search, not opened), long-lived (adult survival of about 92-95% a year, so mortality 800), home range of 1-5 ha (recalled, to confirm), slow reproduction, killed on roads (barriers: built, farmland); densities by cover are placeholders. Blanchard's cricket frog (Acris blanchardi): a small frog of pond and stream edges in the Midwest, in decline (Indiana lists it as a species of special concern per an Indiana DNR search result; the Ohio status is to confirm), a short-lived breeder with high turnover (growth and mortality as the other profile's frog, a placeholder); density, range and dispersal are placeholders. Northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis): the common conspicuous control; territories of about 1-2 ha held by a pair (Cornell Lab, Birds of the World; recalled, to confirm); densities by cover placeholders. Growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection are placeholders, as in the other profile. The Indiana bat (Myotis sodalis), endangered in Ohio, with a summer home range of about 210 ha in a Big Darby Creek (Pickaway County) study (seen in a search snippet only), was considered and left out: its home range is far larger than the modelled landscape.
sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 1.0 USD to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
